verdict: SHIP, matching the pre-registered threshold literally. Q017 is the direct follow-up Q016's own review named as its top priority: does Q016's reflection-forwarding kernel (sourceAssemblies=Assembly.LoadFrom-at-construction + ProvidedParameter/return types derived directly from the real MethodInfo's reflection + invokeCode=fun args -> Expr.Call(realMi, args)) generalize past primitive/single-record signatures to a member with function-typed (FSharpFunc<_,_>) parameters? The pre-registered cheapest falsifier (Round 3) wraps Myriad's own real `map` function ((string->string) -> (int->int) -> Person -> Person, already compiled in Q016's Satellite.dll) as a provided `Map` member and passes real lambda literals at the call site. It PASSES cleanly: 0 compile diagnostics, and the provider-mediated result (name="ADA" age=43 for input ("Ada",42) under uppercase/increment lambdas) agrees field-for-field with an independent direct-reflection call to the real `map` MethodInfo. No new scaffolding beyond Q016's kernel was needed, so REVISE (whose sole trigger is 'passes only after new scaffolding') is out; KILL is out (IL emission accepted the function-typed shape); NULL is out (materially more signature surface than Q016 wrapped). Unlike Q016's review, this review independently rebuilt and reran the spike -- the tooling outage that blocked Q016's reviewer was not in effect. Round 3 reproduced exactly (rebuilt SatelliteTP.Runtime+DesignTime+Harness from the byte-identical checked-in source; also reran Round 1 regression PASS). The review then went past reproduction and built three additional shapes the executor did not test, using the identical kernel: (a) a genuine FSharpFunc<int,int> RETURN value (adder), which flows OUT of the provider and applies correctly (f 100 = 142, agreeing with direct reflection); (b) an FSharpFunc<Person,Person> whose element type is the real record, not a primitive (transform), with a different non-identity lambda, returning name="Ada!" age=420 as expected. Both pass -- so the kernel generalizes further than the single Map case pre-registered. Three qualifications travel with the SHIP: (1) The PASS was predictable, not a discovery. The vendored ProvidedTypes.fs convType (lines 9352-9384) has NO FSharpFunc special-case; FSharpFunc<string,string> takes the same generic-type branch (9365-9369: convert the generic definition, recurse on type arguments, MakeGenericType) as list<int> or Nullable<bool>. Q016's attempt-4 decision to derive types directly from the real MethodInfo's reflection is exactly why it works, and the FSharpFunc-related hits elsewhere in the file (8969-8972 OptimizedClosures arity dispatch; 14456/14469 target-side Expr.Lambda) are in IL/quotation emission, not the parameter-type-conversion path, and never fire for a member that merely declares and forwards an FSharpFunc-typed parameter. Q017's real contribution is turning Q016 review objection-1's hypothesis into a fact verified across four shapes. (2) 'Function-typed' is not load-bearing. The provider forwards function values as opaque object references in both directions and never constructs, adapts, or introspects a closure -- the consumer's lambda is compiled to an FSharpFunc closure class in the consumer assembly and passed as an ordinary argument. The win is exactly as general as 'any reference-typed argument forwards.' (3) The single most important thing 02-results omits: the kernel is brittle to compiled-arity surprises. The reviewer's first `adder` attempt (let adder (r:Person) : (int->int) = fun x -> x + r.age) was flattened by F#'s compiler into a two-parameter method adder(Person,int):int -- no FSharpFunc return at the CLR level at all. The provider built one ProvidedParameter for a two-param method, so Expr.Call threw 'Incorrect number of arguments (Parameter args)' and that single malformed member POISONED THE ENTIRE PROVIDED TYPE (Create/GetName/GetAge/Map/Transform all became 'not defined' in the same compile). There is no per-member isolation. A genuine FSharpFunc return only appeared after defeating the flattener (id (fun x -> ...) to force arity-1). This is a live trap for the Lenses follow-up this result is meant to unblock: a source-level function-returning-function usually compiles to a flat multi-arg method, and the reflection-forwarding provider consumes compiled arity as-is with catastrophic whole-type failure on any mismatch. Top follow-ups, prioritized: (1) before building a Lenses-shaped forwarding provider, check the COMPILED arity of the real Lenses generator's output, since the source signature is not a reliable guide; (2) add arity-mismatch defense (per-member guard/skip-and-warn) to the kernel or document the whole-type-poisoning failure mode; (3) test curried arity>2 with functions interleaved among primitives; (4) real-IDE-host test (standing caveat since Q006 -- all of this is FSharpChecker-as-library). Round 2's file-lock problem is untouched and Q016's REVISE on that axis stands unchanged; this quartet was scoped purely to the generalization question.
